thread:
Soojin Lee: Quote sweep for case studies (Northwind + Helios + Atlas). Dropping the current “quote bank” doc here — please add any customer-approved quotes + flag anything that needs cleanup/approval. https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1redwood-quote-bank

Soojin Lee: Goal: edit for clarity *without changing meaning*. If we change more than punctuation/grammar, we need customer to re-approve.

Ethan Wallace: Adding 6 candidates from my Northwind draft. Pulling from the interview notes + the 10/03 intro call. I’ve marked what I think is “light edit” vs “needs re-approval.”

Ethan Wallace: Northwind candidate quotes:
1) (light edit) “We went from firefighting latency spikes to having predictable p95s we can plan around.”
2) (needs re-approval) “Dedicated let us stop thinking about GPUs and focus on shipping.”
3) (light edit) “The fallback routing was the difference between a SEV-1 and a non-event.”
4) (needs re-approval) “We cut inference cost materially without sacrificing response quality.”

Camila Reyes: ty Ethan. Can we please avoid “stop thinking about GPUs” unless we’re super sure that’s verbatim. Legal will ding us for paraphrasing.

Michael Grant: +1. Rule of thumb: punctuation/grammar = ok. Rephrasing or adding claims = send to customer for approval. Also avoid absolute claims (“eliminated”, “guaranteed”) unless backed by the consent/metrics approval.

Avery Johnson: Northwind is touchy on anything that implies they were “unstable” before. They’re fine with reliability framing, but no “firefighting” language.

Soojin Lee: Good catch. Can we soften #1 to something like “We got more predictable p95 latency…” and remove the implied chaos?

Ethan Wallace: Updated #1 draft:
“Redwood helped us get predictable p95 latency we can plan around.”
That’s still a meaning-preserving edit vs “firefighting”. But since it changes tone, I’ll mark as “send to customer” to be safe.

Rachel Kim: On the CS side: Northwind champion (VP Eng) is ok with reliability angle as long as we don’t reference the specific incident last month. Also they asked we don’t mention competitor-by-name.

Markus Klein: On #3: “fallback routing” is correct technically, but we should say “policy-based routing + fallback” (they used region fallback + smaller model fallback for a subset). I can provide a more precise phrasing that’s still understandable.

Soojin Lee: Markus can you paste your suggested wording? We can try to keep it quote-y (not like marketing copy).

Markus Klein: Suggestion (if customer agrees): “Having routing policies with automatic fallbacks meant brief capacity issues didn’t take the product down.”

Ethan Wallace: I like that. It maps to what they told us, but definitely not verbatim. Will treat as “needs approval.”

Tyler Benson: Tracking ask: when you add quotes to the doc, can you append one of these tags at end of the line?
`[status: verbatim / light edit / needs approval] [owner: name] [customer: Northwind/Helios/Atlas]`
Makes it easier to keep the approval sheet in sync.

Miguel Santos: For Helios, they asked to avoid individual names/titles beyond “Security Lead” (their compliance team didn’t want attribution to a specific person). We may need the quote formatted as “Head of Security, Helios Health” or “Security & Compliance, Helios Health” depending on what Legal signs off on.

Michael Grant: For Helios: if they’re restricting attribution, we can do “Helios Health (Security & Compliance)” *only if* their consent form explicitly allows logo + company name with non-person attribution. Otherwise, anonymized (no logo, no company name) is safer.

Soojin Lee: Helios quote candidates? I only have one that’s usable and it’s a bit stiff.

Miguel Santos: Here’s what I pulled from the 10/07 approvals call notes (close to verbatim but I didn’t transcribe word-for-word):
“Private deployment and audit logging were table stakes for us. We needed to prove who accessed what, when.”
I’ll label as `[needs approval]` since it’s reconstructed.

Ethan Wallace: I’ll rewrite lightly for readability *after* we confirm if it’s verbatim. Otherwise it’s just marketing copy and we’ll get stuck in approval ping-pong.

Avery Johnson: Northwind update: they approved one quote in the email thread (10/04) but asked for two changes:
- Replace “SEV-1” with “major incident”
- Don’t mention “capacity issues” (they prefer “traffic spikes”)
They’re ok with “fallback” wording.

Soojin Lee: Great. Can you paste the exact approved sentence from the email so we can use verbatim?

Avery Johnson: Approved text from Northwind (verbatim from customer email):
“Redwood’s fallback routing helped us keep the assistant online during unexpected traffic spikes.”

Tyler Benson: Logging that as `[status: approved]` in the tracker now. (reaction: :white_check_mark: x2)

Ethan Wallace: Nice. That’s clean and doesn’t overclaim.

Simran Kaur: For Northwind, we also have a strong “devex” quote from the story interview but it includes numbers (“~30% lower p95”) which wasn’t in the metrics approval yet. I suggest we keep a non-metric variant ready:
“Integration was straightforward — we were streaming responses end-to-end in days, not weeks.”
Again: not sure if verbatim.

Camila Reyes: Please keep anything with numbers behind the “metrics approved” gate. We can still collect the exact quote, but don’t put it in the draft page until we have the green light.

Michael Grant: +1. Also, if we publish ranges (“~20–30%”) we need to ensure the consent covers ranges explicitly. Some customers treat ranges as disclosure.

Soojin Lee: Action items:
- Ethan: update quote bank with the Northwind approved sentence + your remaining candidates tagged “needs approval”
- Avery: ask Northwind if they’re ok with a second quote around “predictable p95 latency” (no numbers) and confirm attribution format (name/title/company)
- Miguel: confirm Helios attribution preference (company name ok? anonymized?)
- Tyler: keep tracker updated + drop link here

Tyler Benson: Tracker link (internal): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1redwood-reference-approvals
Tabs: `Quotes`, `Logos`, `Metrics`.

Rachel Kim: Reminder on CS guardrails: max 2 reference asks in a week per customer. If we need additional quote approvals, batch them and send once. (reaction: :thumbsup: x3)

Ethan Wallace: Added to quote bank + tagged per Tyler’s format. Also added a “DO NOT EDIT” section with verbatim approved quotes so we don’t accidentally tweak later.

Soojin Lee: Perfect. Once we have Helios attribution confirmed, I’ll finalize the callout blocks for the case study template + send to Legal for a quick read. (reaction: :eyes: x2)

Michael Grant: When you send the final set, include:
- exact quote text
- attribution line
- where it will appear (web page / PDF / deck)
- whether logo is shown in same asset
That avoids back-and-forth.

Avery Johnson: Northwind reply just came in: attribution ok as “Nadia P., VP Engineering, Northwind Commerce” and they’re fine with logo on the case study page, but want a 5 business day review window before publish.

Camila Reyes: Great. Please add the 5-day review window note to the approvals tracker so we don’t miss it during the publish sprint.

Tyler Benson: Done. `[Northwind | review window: 5 biz days | owner: Avery]` added. (reaction: :white_check_mark: x1)
